title: Rocks and Minerals
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Rocks and Minerals Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the properties of minerals (hardness, colour, streak, lustre); identify igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks and how they form; describe uses of rocks and minerals and the effects of mining in Ontario. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Rocks, Minerals, and Erosion)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on minerals, the Mohs hardness scale, streak and lustre, igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks and their uses. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Igneous rocks cool from magma; sedimentary rocks form in layers; metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rocks are made of one or more minerals. Minerals are natural, non-living solids.

  • Minerals are identified by hardness (Mohs scale, talc 1 to diamond 10), colour, streak and lustre.
  • Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools (granite, basalt).
  • Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment pressed together (sandstone, limestone) and may hold fossils.
  • Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change rocks (marble, slate).
Example

A mineral scratches quartz. What do you know?

harder minerals scratch softer ones

Answer: it is harder than quartz

Example

Which rock type might have fossils?

fossils form in sediment layers

Answer: sedimentary

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a mineral's outside colour always matches its streak.
  • Mixing up rocks and minerals.
  • Thinking fossils are found in igneous rocks.

faq.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
faq.a: A mineral is one natural solid substance. A rock is made of one or more minerals.

faq.q: How do we test the hardness of a mineral?
faq.a: Try to scratch it with objects of known hardness, such as a fingernail, a copper coin, a steel nail and glass.

faq.q: Why is mining important in Ontario?
faq.a: Ontario mines nickel, gold and other minerals used in batteries, coins and buildings. Mines must be cleaned up to protect the land.

items.q: Quartz is 7 on the Mohs scale and calcite is 3. Which one can scratch the other?

items.q: Which of these is a fossil: a feather found in the garden, a piece of brick, a seashell washed up today or a trilobite in a slab of rock?
c: a trilobite in a slab of rock
a feather found in the garden
items.e: A fossil is the remains or trace of a living thing from long ago, preserved in rock.

items.q: Layer A has a coral fossil. What does this tell you about the area when layer A formed?
c: The area has always looked the same.
The area was always covered by ice.
The area was once dry land with plants or animals living on it.
The area was once covered by ocean water.
items.e: A coral fossil is evidence that the area was once covered by ocean water.

items.q: Why do scientists say the Grand Canyon took millions of years to form?

items.q: Why are there so few fossils of jellyfish?
c: Jellyfish have no hard parts, so they usually rot away.
items.e: Hard parts last.

items.q: The rock layers have not been turned over. Which layer is younger, layer B or layer C?
items.e: Layer C is lower than layer B, so it is older.

items.q: Nathan sees the same three layers in two cliffs across a valley. What can he conclude?
c: The valley is older than the layers.
The layers are different ages on each side.
The layers were once connected, and the valley was carved later.
The cliffs formed in different places.
items.e: Matching patterns show the layers formed together.

items.q: A footprint fossil is found. What can it tell scientists?
c: the size of the animal and how it walked
items.e: Trace fossils show behaviour.

items.q: The rock layers have not been turned over. Which layer is younger, layer A or layer C?
items.e: Layer C is lower than layer A, so it is older.

items.q: Why do old gravestones made of limestone become hard to read?

items.e: Weathering.

items.q: Why would chalk be a poor choice for a doorstep?

items.e: Choose hard rock for steps.

items.q: Fossil seashells are found high in the hills. What does this tell us?
c: The land was once under the sea.
items.e: Fossils are clues.

items.q: Which fossil is older: the clam or the fish?

items.e: The fish is in a lower layer, so it is older.

items.q: Why do pebbles on a beach become smooth and rounded?

items.q: The bottom layer has a tree leaf fossil. The top layer has a coral fossil. How did this area change over time?

It was dry land first and later became covered by ocean.
items.e: Bottom layers are older. The tree leaf (older) shows dry land; the coral (younger) shows covered by ocean.
